Z14-P63:action1 Wash and trim fresh young vegetables cleanly, then **blanch** most vegetables in vigorously boiling water (or steam per exact NCHFP table) for the exact crop-specific minutes—blanching stops natural enzymes that otherwise turn unblanched frozen vegetables woody, gray, and hay-flavored within weeks.
Z14-P63:action2 Immediately transfer blanched vegetables into an abundant **ICE-WATER BATH** for the EXACT same number of minutes they were blanched so cooking stops instantly instead of turning vegetables mushy.
Z14-P63:action3 Drain thoroughly on clean towels before packaging (excess surface water forms heavy frost crystals and freezer burn), noting that small quantities of raw peppers, onions, or herbs may be frozen unblanched per NCHFP if used cooked.
Z14-P63:failure Freezing raw unblanched garden green beans and sweet corn straight in thin sandwich bags, resulting in tough off-flavored freezer-burned produce by December.
Z14-P63:verify Confirm exact NCHFP crop blanch time followed, equal-duration ice-water chill completed, and produce drained dry before bagging.
Z14-P63:stop Water failing to return to a boil within 1 minute after dropping vegetables indicates the batch is too large for the pot—split into smaller 1-pound batches.
Z14-P64:action1 Pack foods strictly in thick **moisture-vapor-resistant** freezer bags, freezer paper, or rigid freezer-grade containers (NOT thin bread bags, milk cartons, or flimsy deli tubs that leak air and cause dry leathery freezer burn), pressing excess air cleanly out before sealing.
Z14-P64:action2 Leave proper liquid **expansion headspace** (typically ½ to 1½ inches depending on container width and liquid content) so freezing soups, stocks, and sauces expand cleanly without bursting rigid containers or shattering wide-mouth straight-sided freezer jars (never freeze liquids in narrow-shoulder canning jars!).
Z14-P64:action3 Freeze packages in a single spaced layer against cold freezer walls/shelves at **0°F or below**—avoid overloading a freezer with more than roughly 2 to 3 pounds of unfrozen food per cubic foot in 24 hours so cores freeze rapidly instead of lingering in the Danger Zone.
Z14-P64:failure Stacking 40 pounds of warm soup quarts tight together inside a chest freezer, taking three days to freeze while centers sour.
Z14-P64:verify Confirm freezer-rated packaging, air pressed out, liquid headspace left, date/content labeled clearly, and freezer holds ≤0°F.
Z14-P64:stop Freezer temperatures rising above 0°F during heavy loading require pausing new warm additions until existing loads freeze solid.
Z14-P65:action1 Thaw frozen meats, poultry, seafood, and prepared meals using ONLY one of three USDA-validated safe methods: **1) Refrigerator thawing** (slow, safest—place on a rimmed tray on the bottom shelf at ≤40°F), **2) Cold-water thawing** (sealed leak-proof bag submerged in cold tap water changed every 30 minutes, cooking immediately once thawed), or **3) Microwave thawing** (cooking immediately afterward).
Z14-P65:action2 NEVER thaw frozen meats, poultry, or cooked casseroles on the kitchen counter, in hot water, or in a warm sunny garage—the outer surface rapidly warms past 40°F into the bacterial Danger Zone hours before the icy center melts.
Z14-P65:action3 Remember that freezing pauses bacteria without killing them; foods thawed in the refrigerator may be safely refrozen (with slight quality loss), whereas foods thawed in cold water or a microwave MUST be fully cooked first before any refreezing.
Z14-P65:failure Setting a frozen five-pound roast on the kitchen counter at 7 a.m. to thaw all day until dinner at 6 p.m.
Z14-P65:verify Confirm refrigerator bottom-tray thaw, 30-minute cold-water swaps + immediate cook, or microwave + immediate cook—zero counter thawing.
Z14-P65:stop Perishable meat or meal left thawing at room temperature longer than 2 hours (1 hour >90°F) must be discarded cleanly.
Z14-P75:action3 Inspect dry goods periodically—freeze newly purchased dry flour/grains cleanly at 0°F for 3 to 4 days if desired to kill hidden pantry-moth/weevil eggs before moving into sealed storage jars.
Z14-P79:stop Overwhelming harvest volumes exceeding safe tested processing time should be shared fresh with neighbors/food shelves or frozen cleanly rather than cutting canning corners.

Z14-P70:action1 Use ONLY commercially standardized **5% acidity vinegar** (check the bottle label—many specialty/rice/diluted vinegars sit at 4% or lower and are UNSAFE for shelf-stable canning!), and NEVER dilute the vinegar-to-water ratio stated in the tested USDA/NCHFP recipe to make pickles "less sour."

Z14-P71:action1 Weigh cabbage/produce and pure **canning/pickling salt** accurately per a tested USDA/NCHFP fermentation recipe—exact salt concentration suppresses bad bacteria while letting beneficial Lactobacillus produce preserving lactic acid cleanly.
Z14-P71:action2 Use ONLY clean food-grade glass, food-grade plastic (HDPE #2), or lead-free stoneware crocks (NEVER galvanized metal, copper, aluminum, chipped ceramic, or garbage bags—acidic brine dissolves toxic zinc/lead/plasticizers straight into food!).
Z14-P71:action3 Keep ALL vegetables continuously **SUBMERGED 1 to 2 inches beneath liquid brine** using clean food-grade weights (glass weights or heavy food-grade brine-filled freezer bags—never limestone rocks that dissolve in acid!), fermenting at controlled NCHFP temperatures (roughly 70–75°F for 3–4 weeks for sauerkraut; avoid hot >80°F rooms that spoil ferments).
Z14-P71:failure Fermenting sauerkraut in a galvanized metal tub weighted down with a backyard limestone rock in an 88°F garage.
Z14-P71:verify Confirm food-grade non-reactive vessel, exact weighed canning salt, vegetables fully submerged under brine, and controlled 68–75°F fermentation temp.
Z14-P71:stop Hot >80°F fermentation rooms, reactive metal/leaded vessels, or dry exposed vegetables rising above brine require discarding failed batches cleanly.
Z14-P72:action1 Use the spoilage and storage criteria from the exact tested ferment. If mold, abnormal odor or texture, or process deviation raises doubt, stop and seek Extension advice. Never taste to check safety.
Z14-P72:action2 Recognize clear spoilage failure cues: **fuzzy colored mold** (black, blue, green, pink, or heavy fuzzy white mats growing on exposed vegetables or brine), **slimy ropy brine**, mushy soft hollow pickles, darkened brown/pink discoloration, or putrid/rotten/cheesy odors.
Z14-P72:action3 Discard ANY moldy, slimy, mushy, or foul-smelling ferment completely—mycotoxins and off-pathogens penetrate liquid brine far deeper than visible surface mold; once a healthy ferment finishes cleanly, move it promptly to cold refrigerator storage (≤40°F) OR process per a tested NCHFP boiling-water recipe.

Z14-P72:verify Confirm crisp texture, clean tangy aroma, zero colored/fuzzy mold or slime, and timely transfer to ≤40°F cold storage or tested canning.
Z14-P72:stop Any sliminess, rotten odor, pink/black discoloration, or fuzzy mold halts consumption immediately—discard and wash/sanitize the vessel thoroughly.

Z14-P14:action2 Grow foods your household ACTUALLY eats and knows how to cook and preserve—an acre of unfamiliar root crops or unpreserved zucchini goes to waste during emergencies.
Z14-P14:verify Confirm crop mix matches household meals, northern maturity dates, and available curing/cellar/preservation capacity.
Z14-P14:stop Do not assume a backyard residential plot alone replaces full household nutrition; treat home production as a high-value supplement paired with rotated pantry reserves.
Z14-P33:action2 Remove any softening or blemished item IMMEDIATELY, wipe adjacent dry produce cleanly if damp, and plan household meals around items nearing the end of their natural storage window ("eat the ripest/oldest first").
Z14-P60:action3 Rotate home-canned foods strictly First-In, First-Out (FIFO) and plan for best nutritional and seal quality within roughly **1 year**—never promise arbitrary 10-to-25-year safe shelf lives for home-canned jars.
Z14-P73:action1 Stock familiar, everyday shelf-stable foods that require **NO refrigeration and MINIMAL water or cooking**: canned meats, fish, beans, soups, vegetables, and fruits, peanut/nut butters, crackers, oats, dry pasta/rice (when fuel/water exist), shelf-stable UHT milk, and comfort snacks—paired with a sturdy **manual can opener**.
Z14-P73:action2 Avoid salty/spicy foods that spike drinking-water demand sharply during water outages, and skip buying exotic "emergency buckets" nobody in the household has ever tasted or verified against food allergies.
Z14-P73:action3 Practice **FIFO (First-In, First-Out)** rotation seamlessly as part of normal grocery shopping: mark purchase/expiration dates boldly on can tops, place newly bought items at the BACK of the shelf, and cook from the FRONT so reserves stay fresh continuously with zero expired waste.
Z14-P73:failure Buying three cases of unfamiliar emergency ration bars ten years ago and forgetting a manual can opener when a blackout shuts off the electric opener.
Z14-P73:verify Confirm manual can opener staged with pantry, low-salt familiar no-cook meals included, dates marked boldly, and FIFO rotation active.
Z14-P73:stop Do not rely on single-ingredient dry staples (like raw dry beans alone) without matching water, soaking time, and safe outdoor cooking fuel.
Z14-P74:action2 Segregate dedicated allergen-free (nut-free, gluten-free, dairy-free) or clinical-diet emergency foods (low-sodium, diabetic-friendly snacks, dysphagia soft foods) clearly in separate labeled bins—community disaster shelters often cannot guarantee safe specialized allergen meals.
Z14-P74:action3 Store at least 7 to 14+ days of dry/canned pet and service-animal food (plus manual can opener and extra pet drinking water) inside rigid chew-proof bins rotated on the exact same FIFO schedule.
Z14-P74:failure Discovering during a 5-day blizzard that the emergency pantry consists entirely of peanut butter and wheat pasta while a child has celiac disease and nut allergy.
Z14-P74:verify Confirm ready-to-feed infant formula or extra safe mixing water, segregated allergen/medical bins, and dedicated pet/service-animal food rotated fresh.
Z14-P74:stop Exhausting specialized infant formula or critical medical-diet supplies during an extended outage requires contacting local public-health/emergency agencies early before stocks run out.
Z14-P76:action1 Inspect EVERY commercial can carefully before opening: **DISCARD IMMEDIATELY** any can that is **bulging/swollen** at the ends, **leaking or spurting** when punctured, **deeply dented right on a top/bottom seam or side crease** (sharp dents break the hermetic double seam!), or **heavily rusted** enough to pit through the metal.
Z14-P76:action2 Wipe dusty commercial can lids clean with a damp cloth BEFORE cutting open so pantry dust and rodent residue never fall directly into the food, and wash the manual can-opener blade cleanly after use.
Z14-P76:action3 Recognize that a minor shallow smooth dent on the flat side wall AWAY from seams generally leaves the seal intact if unswollen and unrusted—whereas ANY seam crease, sharp point dent, or bulge is an automatic zero-taste discard.

Z14-P76:stop Swollen, spurting, foaming, foul-smelling, or seam-compromised commercial cans must be discarded cleanly without tasting.
Z14-P77:action1 Understand U.S. commercial food-date labels accurately: **"Best if Used By"** and **"Sell By"** on intact, properly stored shelf-stable cans/boxes reflect peak manufacturer flavor and texture QUALITY—NOT an automatic safety cutoff—with the critical mandatory exception of **INFANT FORMULA**, which MUST NEVER be used past its printed "Use By" date (nutrient degradation and safety risk).
Z14-P77:action2 Reject exaggerated marketing or internet claims promising universal 20-to-30-year safe shelf lives for home-canned jars, ordinary grocery cans, or uncontrolled warm pantries—acidic canned foods (tomatoes, pineapple, pickles) corrode can linings faster (~12–18 months quality) while low-acid intact commercial cans hold longer (~2–5 years quality) in cool dry storage.
Z14-P77:action3 Combine intact physical package inspection + cool dry 50–70°F storage + active FIFO grocery rotation so household reserves stay both safe AND deliciously nutritious.
Z14-P77:failure Feeding expired infant formula during an outage OR hoarding home-canned tomatoes for ten years in a hot closet assuming "sealed means immortal."
Z14-P77:verify Confirm infant formula strictly within Use-By date, acidic vs low-acid commercial quality windows respected, and active FIFO rotation running.
Z14-P77:stop Expired infant formula, compromised cans, rancid fats, or unsealed home jars are NEVER safe regardless of date labels.
Z14-P78:action1 Prioritize **no-cook** ready-to-eat pantry meals first (canned beans/chicken/tuna, nut butter wraps, canned fruit, oats soaked in water/UHT milk) to conserve both cooking fuel and dishwashing water during outages.
Z14-P78:action2 If heating food during an electrical blackout, operate portable camp stoves, propane grills, or charcoal grills **STRICTLY OUTDOORS** in completely open air well away from siding, overhangs, garages, and open windows—NEVER heat food over camp stoves, charcoal, or Sterno-bank fires in unventilated indoor rooms (lethal CO and fire hazard).
Z14-P78:action3 Cook ONLY single-meal portions during outages when refrigeration is dead—leftover heated meats, beans, or rice cannot be safely kept overnight at room temperature and spoil within 2 hours.
Z14-P78:verify Confirm no-cook meals prioritized, any fuel-stove cooking happens strictly outdoors in open air, and single-meal portions leave zero warm leftovers.

Z14-P79:action3 Record honest annual lessons (which crops thrived, which jars got eaten first, where storage temperatures drifted) so each year's household food plan grows simpler, safer, and less wasteful.

Z15-P58:action2 Eat household food in smart spoilage order across weeks: **1)** Safe-temp refrigerated perishables first, **2)** Safe frozen items if power fails, **3)** Root-cellar/fresh produce showing early age, and **4)** Rotated shelf-stable canned and dry pantry staples last.

Z10-P69:action2 Monitor older adults closely for blunted thirst/cold sensation, balance/fall hazards, blood-thinner bleeding risks (minor head bumps can cause serious delayed bleeding), and heat-wave medication sensitivity.
Z13-P59:action2 During extended sub-zero freezes, extreme heat waves, or multi-day blackouts, perform brief safe daytime wellness checks (confirming indoor warmth/cooling, working CO alarms, water, medications, and charged comms) without forcing entry or risking icy travel hazards.
Z13-P64:action2 Track indoor temperature objectively with a thermometer during multi-day outages—relocating BEFORE indoor winter air plunges into hypothermia/pipe-freeze territory (especially with infants, older adults, or chronic illness) or before indoor summer heat traps dangerous heat-stroke temperatures without cooling.
Z15-P33:stop Indoor room temperatures climbing to unsafe heat-wave levels inside a sealed clean room require prioritizing heat-stroke safety via air-conditioned clean-air shelters.
Z15-P34:action2 If your home lacks air conditioning (or power fails) during simultaneous smoke and extreme heat, relocate proactively to a public air-conditioned clean-air cooling center, library, mall, or cooled relative's home—taking vulnerable elders, infants, and asthmatics early.
Z15-P34:failure Keeping every window sealed tight in a 98°F third-floor un-air-conditioned apartment to block smoke haze while an elderly resident develops fatal heat stroke.
Z15-P34:verify Confirm indoor temperature monitored alongside AQI, AC recirculate mode verified, and air-conditioned shelter relocation triggered early if indoor heat spikes.
Z15-P37:action1 Monitor both daytime **Heat Index** (temperature + humidity) AND **overnight minimum temperatures**—when nighttime air stays above 75–80°F in un-air-conditioned homes, bodies never shed stored daytime heat, causing cumulative organ stress across days 2 through 5 of a heat wave.
Z15-P37:action2 Reschedule outdoor work, athletics, and errands strictly to early morning before peak sun, draw shades/blinds on sun-facing windows early, avoid running home ovens, wear light loose breathable clothes, and hydrate steadily with safe water before thirst lags.
Z15-P37:action3 Check TWICE DAILY on older adults, infants, pregnant individuals, outdoor workers, and neighbors taking heat-sensitive medications (such as diuretics or certain psychiatric/heart drugs).
Z15-P37:failure Ignoring day three of a humid heat wave in an upstairs apartment because daytime air dropped two degrees while indoor walls radiate 92°F heat all night.
Z15-P37:verify Confirm live NWS heat alerts monitored, sun-facing blinds shut early, exertion shifted to dawn, and vulnerable neighbors checked twice daily.
Z15-P37:stop Indoor living temperatures climbing into dangerous heat stress without working AC triggers immediate relocation to an air-conditioned cooling center.
Z15-P38:action3 Preserve grid stability safely when utilities issue conservation appeals only within safe indoor temperatures—never turn AC off for frail, elderly, or heat-vulnerable household members during Excessive Heat Warnings.
Z15-P38:failure Leaving a frail older adult in a 98°F closed apartment with a single oscillating floor fan believing the moving air prevents heat stroke.
Z15-P39:action1 NEVER leave a child, dependent adult, or pet alone inside a parked vehicle for even **"just two minutes"**—greenhouse solar heating spikes cabin temperatures by roughly 20°F in 10 minutes and can reach fatal temperatures above 120°F even when outdoor air is a mild 70°F and windows are cracked open.
Z15-P39:action2 Build automatic fail-safe habits to defeat routine-change memory slips: place your purse, work badge, lunch bag, or left shoe right beside the rear child car seat, ALWAYS open the back door to look before locking, and keep parked cars locked at home so toddlers cannot climb inside unattended.
Z15-P39:action3 If you ever see a child or pet locked alone in a hot parked car showing distress or unresponsiveness, call **911 IMMEDIATELY** and follow dispatcher/Good Samaritan legal guidance to get them out and begin immediate rapid cooling.
Z15-P39:failure Cracking car windows an inch in a 75°F sunny parking lot for ten minutes while running into a store with a sleeping toddler or dog in back.
Z15-P39:verify Confirm back-seat look-before-lock habit active on every drive, parked vehicles locked at home, and zero unattended minutes tolerated.
Z15-P39:stop Any child, adult, or pet left inside a hot vehicle is an immediate life-threatening emergency requiring urgent rescue and 911 medical cooling.
Z15-P40:action1 Identify nearby public **cooling centers** (public libraries, community centers, senior centers, malls, county emergency cooling sites via 211 or local broadcast radio) BEFORE peak afternoon temperatures hit, checking accessible transit and pet/service-animal rules in advance.
Z15-P40:action2 Plan spending the hottest peak hours (roughly 11 a.m. to 6 p.m.) inside air-conditioned spaces whenever home cooling fails—just several continuous hours in cool AC dramatically lowers cumulative cardiovascular and kidney strain.
Z15-P40:action3 Check in by phone or brief daytime door knock at least TWICE DAILY on older neighbors, people living alone, and households without AC—summoning 911 promptly if someone fails to answer or appears flushed, confused, or dizzy.
Z15-P40:failure Staying isolated inside a top-floor un-air-conditioned bedroom through day four of an Excessive Heat Warning without telling family or visiting a free library cooling center.
Z15-P40:verify Confirm local cooling-center hours/transit verified via 211/radio and twice-daily neighbor/relative check-ins active during heat waves.
Z15-P40:stop Confusion, slurred speech, collapse, or unanswered welfare check during extreme heat triggers immediate 911 activation.
Z15-P41:action1 Treat ANY sudden confusion, slurred speech, stumbling, agitation, seizure, fainting, or hot skin during a heat wave as **LIFE-THREATENING HEAT STROKE**—call **911 IMMEDIATELY** and move the person into shade or air conditioning without delay.

exact_operational_assertions:
Z13-P65:action2 Leave EARLY during safe daylight and passable road conditions rather than waiting until midnight blizzards or flood crests isolate your neighborhood; verify county road closures (e.g., Minnesota 511) before driving.
Z13-P65:failure Waiting until 11 p.m. in a whiteout when indoor temperature hits 42°F and getting stranded in a ditch halfway to a closed shelter.
Z13-P65:stop Impassable blizzard whiteouts or active flash floods prohibit driving—hold safely inside until authorities clear roads, or call 911 if an immediate life threat develops indoors.
Z15-P04:action1 Align seasonal staging with Upper Midwest risk windows: **Spring** (rapid snowmelt river flooding, ice jams, early severe storms), **Summer** (tornadoes, straight-line derechos, flash floods, extreme heat domes, regional wildfire smoke plumes), **Autumn** (early wet snow/windstorms, harvest fire/smoke), and **Winter** (blizzards, freezing-rain ice storms, extreme wind-chill blackouts).
Z15-P04:failure Leaving winter blankets, snow shovel, and jumper gear out of the car trunk until late November and getting stranded in an early-season freezing sleet storm.
Z15-P09:action1 Complete errands EARLY on Winter Storm Watch days: top off vehicle fuel tanks, fill critical prescription refills, stage stored drinking water and no-cook pantry foods, fully charge all phones/power banks/medical batteries, and bring a snow shovel and ice-melt/sand inside near the door.
Z15-P09:action2 Clear gutters/downspouts before freezing-rain ice storms, check exterior furnace/dryer vent locations, test smoke and CO alarms, and confirm family warming-center backup options before whiteouts begin.
Z15-P09:action3 Cancel non-essential travel completely once a Blizzard Warning or Ice Storm Warning takes effect—highway closures and multi-vehicle pileups trap drivers far faster than plows can clear drifts.
Z15-P09:failure Driving to the grocery store after freezing rain begins coating overhead tree limbs and roadways, sliding into a ditch as power lines snap.
Z15-P09:verify Confirm vehicle fueled, meds/water/batteries topped off, alarms tested, and non-essential trips cancelled pre-onset.
Z15-P09:stop Active Blizzard Warnings, freezing-rain glaze, or state DOT "No Travel Advised" orders halt road departure immediately.
Z15-P10:action1 Stay INDOORS away from ice-loaded trees and sagging overhead utility lines during and immediately after an ice storm—even light wind gusts hours after rain stops snap heavy frozen limbs and energized high-voltage cables unpredictably.
Z15-P10:action2 Recognize that widespread ice storms break thousands of utility poles simultaneously, routinely producing **3-to-14-day blackouts** across rural and suburban feeders—conserve battery power immediately, seal off one interior warm room with zero indoor combustion, and monitor indoor temperature closely.
Z15-P10:failure Walking outside under cracking ice-coated oak limbs to drag a fallen branch off a downed neighborhood wire.
Z15-P10:verify Confirm family stays indoors away from heavy ice-glazed trees/wires, warm-room insulation active, and relocation threshold monitored.
Z15-P10:stop Indoor freezing temps, exhausted medical batteries, or a tree crashing onto the roof/utility mast triggers immediate safe exit away from wires and calling 911.
Z15-P12:action1 Check live state DOT road reports (such as Minnesota 511) AND NWS forecasts BEFORE leaving—Remember clear blue sky plus 35 mph wind over open farmland still generates zero-visibility ground blizzards and black-ice whiteouts.
Z15-P12:action2 Keep winter gas tanks above HALF-FULL at all times and pack a real winter trunk kit (wool blankets/sleeping bags, dry hats/mittens, metal shovel, traction sand/cat litter, tow strap, jumper pack, headlamp, snacks, water, high-visibility cloth).
Z15-P12:action3 Exit early into a safe open town, motel, or rest stop the moment visibility drops, wipers freeze solid, or plows pull off the road—NEVER push past closed-road gates or follow tail lights blindly into whiteouts.
Z15-P12:failure Driving past a "Road Closed" winter gate on a rural highway at dusk trying to beat a blizzard home, getting buried in a six-foot snowdrift.
Z15-P12:verify Confirm 511 road status open, fuel >half-tank, full winter trunk kit loaded, and someone knows your route and ETA before departing.
Z15-P12:stop Freezing rain glaze, zero-visibility whiteout, or DOT "No Travel Advised" / closed gates mandate halting immediately at the nearest safe town.
Z15-P13:action1 **STAY WITH YOUR VEHICLE** if stranded in a winter storm unless a clearly visible, open, heated building is literally yards away—wandering on foot into blowing snow disorients travelers within seconds and causes fatal hypothermia.
Z15-P14:action1 Recognize that heavy wet snow shoveling in freezing air spikes heart rate and blood pressure dramatically—push snow rather than lifting heavy loads, take small scoops, pace slowly with frequent warm indoor breaks, stay hydrated, and let younger/fitter helpers or hired plows clear driveways for older adults or anyone with heart history.
Z15-P14:action2 Clear exterior furnace/water-heater PVC exhaust vents, fire hydrants near the curb, and primary exit doors FIRST before tackling full driveways—and NEVER stick hands or feet inside a clogged snowblower chute (always shut the engine completely OFF and use a wooden clearing stick!).
Z15-P14:action3 Watch overhead for hanging icicles and sliding roof snow avalanches when clearing walkways right along building eaves.
Z15-P14:failure Rushing out at dawn with known high blood pressure to heave waist-deep wet snow nonstop, ignoring chest tightness and shortness of breath.
Z15-P14:verify Confirm exterior exhaust vents and exit doors cleared first, slow push-and-rest pacing used, and zero hands placed near snowblower chutes.
Z15-P15:action1 Monitor county emergency management, local AM/FM radio, or dial **211** (where active) as soon as a prolonged winter outage begins so you know exact community warming-center addresses, hours (daytime vs overnight), accessibility features, and pet policies BEFORE nightfall.
Z15-P15:action2 Trigger departure proactively during safe daylight if indoor temperatures trend steadily downward toward unsafe cold (especially with infants, older adults, or medically fragile occupants) rather than waiting for midnight emergencies.
Z15-P15:failure Waiting until indoor temperature hits 36°F at 2 a.m. in a blizzard only to find the nearest daytime library warming center closed at 6 p.m.
Z15-P15:stop If impassable blizzard roads make driving unsafe while indoor heat fails and life safety is threatened, call 911 for coordinated emergency rescue rather than driving into whiteouts.
Z15-P50:action2 **SHELTER IN PLACE** when moving outside exposes occupants to greater immediate danger than staying inside—such as active Tornado Warnings, lightning/derecho squalls, blinding whiteout blizzards, impassable flash floods, or official short-term hazmat Shelter-in-Place orders.
Z15-P50:action3 Re-evaluate continuously as conditions evolve: a safe blizzard shelter-in-place on Day 1 can shift into a necessary daylight warming-center evacuation on Day 3 once roads plow open and indoor temperatures fall.
Z16-P13:action1 Open Z15-P13 for shelter safely inside a stranded winter vehicle and guard against exhaust CO; Z15-P14 for avoid snow-shoveling cardiac strain and manage post-blizzard exterior hazards.
audit_note: Retained the A02 substantive concern and checked current references. General storm prep supported. Winter vehicle idling, medical support and restoration require exact conditions.

Z13-P66:action2 Plan for multi-story building dependencies: elevators fail immediately (never use elevators during storms/fires—know both enclosed stairwell exits), municipal upper-floor water booster pumps can fail during outages, and hallways rely on short-duration emergency lights.
Z13-P67:action1 Recognize that rural distribution feeders often restore LAST after widespread ice storms and wind events—plan extended drinking-water, sanitation, food, and warming contingencies well beyond urban 72-hour baselines.
Z15-P06:action2 Keep a modest reserve of **small-denomination cash** ($1s, $5s, $10s, $20s) stored securely at home—regional blackouts shut down ATMs, bank branches, and retail credit-card terminals immediately, and stores often cannot make change for large bills.
Z15-P06:failure Evacuating a wildfire or flood with zero paper IDs, zero prescription list, and $0 cash while regional card networks and cloud portals stay offline for four days.
Z15-P10:action2 Recognize that widespread ice storms break thousands of utility poles simultaneously, routinely producing **3-to-14-day blackouts** across rural and suburban feeders—conserve battery power immediately, seal off one interior warm room with zero indoor combustion, and monitor indoor temperature closely.
Z15-P42:action1 Map the cascading chain BEFORE storms hit: when regional power drops, **gas-station fuel pumps stop**, **ATMs and credit-card terminals go offline**, **cell-tower backup batteries drain within hours to a day**, **elevators and residential well/septic pumps stop**, and **municipal water pressure may drop** triggering Boil Water notices.
Z15-P42:action2 Build simple everyday habits that buffer cascading failures automatically: keep vehicle fuel above **HALF-TANK** year-round, maintain small-denomination cash, keep stored potable water and FIFO pantry food ready, and store critical phone numbers and medication lists on paper.
Z15-P42:action3 Understand utility restoration order realistically: crews clear life-threatening downed wires first, then restore high-voltage transmission lines, substations, hospitals/water plants, main feeders, and finally isolated residential tap lines—so individual rural or side-street homes can wait days longer than downtown corridors.
Z15-P42:failure Waiting until a regional derecho cuts power across five counties to drive on an empty gas tank to an ATM and grocery store.
Z15-P42:verify Confirm half-tank fuel habit, small cash staged, stored water independent of electric pumps, and paper contact binder ready.
Z15-P42:stop Cascading utility losses combining dead heat/cooling, lost water, and failing medical power trigger early relocation outside the affected grid zone.
Z15-P47:action1 Adopt the simple **"Half-Tank Is Empty"** rule year-round—refueling every household vehicle whenever gauges near half-full guarantees immediate 150-to-250+ mile evacuation range even if a sudden blackout shuts down every local gas station pump overnight.
Z15-P47:action2 Keep small-denomination physical cash ($1s, $5s, $10s, $20s) stored securely alongside vital documents so you can purchase food, ice, lodging, or fuel at generator-backed rural stores when broadband card terminals and ATMs stay dark.
Z15-P47:failure Waiting until a Hurricane/Blizzard Warning hits to queue at empty gas stations with 1/8 tank left and zero cash while card networks fail.
Z15-P47:verify Confirm household vehicles routinely refuel at half-tank, small cash bills staged safely, and zero fuel stored inside vehicle cabins/homes.
Z15-P47:stop Driving an evacuation vehicle into an active disaster zone below quarter-tank without confirmed open fuel stations ahead risks stranding.
audit_note: Retained the A02 substantive concern and checked current references. Outages can disrupt critical services. Duration and infrastructure failure cannot be predicted from the source.

Z13-P15:action1 Remember that Wi-Fi routers, VoIP modems, and AC-powered cordless home telephone bases die IMMEDIATELY when house electricity fails—keep cell phones in low-power mode and use short SMS text messages rather than voice calls when towers congest.
Z13-P58:action3 Preserve smartphone battery aggressively (airplane mode between scheduled check-ins, dimmed screen, text SMS instead of streaming video) so phones stay alive for true 911 emergencies and brief family text check-ins.
Z13-P58:failure Draining every family smartphone to 0% scrolling social media during the first four hours of a three-day winter blackout.
Z15-P05:action1 Designate ONE **out-of-area emergency contact** (relative or friend living in another state/region outside the local disaster zone)—during regional disasters, local calls often jam while brief SMS texts to an out-of-area number still get through so everyone checks in through one hub.
Z15-P05:action2 Agree on TWO physical meeting places BEFORE an emergency: **1) Neighborhood rally point** right outside your block (for house fires or gas leaks), and **2) Out-of-neighborhood or out-of-town rally point** (library, school, relative's home) if police block entry to your street.
Z15-P05:action3 Put a laminated paper contact card (names, phones, rally addresses, medical allergies, school pick-up authorization) in every adult wallet and child backpack so no one depends on a dead smartphone screen.
Z15-P05:failure Losing cell service during a midday tornado while family members drive to opposite sides of town guessing where everyone else went.
Z15-P05:verify Confirm every member carries a paper contact card, knows the out-of-area relay, and has walked or viewed both physical rally points.
Z15-P05:stop Never drive into active law-enforcement road closures or live hazard zones trying to locate family—check in via the out-of-area contact and designated rally point.
Z15-P46:action1 Switch from voice calls to **short SMS text messages** immediately during regional disasters—voice circuits jam within minutes while brief texts queue and slip through congested towers using minimal phone battery.
Z15-P46:action2 Keep phones in Airplane Mode or Low-Power Mode between scheduled check-in windows, disable auto-sync/video streaming, and check local official AM/FM and NOAA Weather Radio broadcasts for county updates and alternate emergency dispatch numbers if 911 lines experience local outages.
Z15-P46:action3 Note that Text-to-911 availability varies by county (call voice 911 first whenever possible; use Text-to-911 only where supported or if unable to speak)—and if ALL phone networks fail completely during a life-threatening emergency, know the physical address of your nearest staffed fire station, police precinct, or hospital.
Z15-P46:failure Making twenty frantic back-to-back voice calls on a congested network until the battery dies before an important evacuation update arrives.
Z15-P46:verify Confirm SMS priority habit, paper address of nearest fire station/hospital logged, and battery NOAA/AM-FM radios active.
Z15-P46:stop Medically fragile households facing complete loss of 911 access during an active hazard should relocate early to a staffed serviced area.

exact_operational_assertions:
Z13-P65:action1 Identify at least TWO pre-arranged relocation destinations BEFORE storm season (a powered friend/relative outside your immediate utility feeder plus official county/municipal warming or cooling centers announced via local radio/211).
Z13-P65:action2 Leave EARLY during safe daylight and passable road conditions rather than waiting until midnight blizzards or flood crests isolate your neighborhood; verify county road closures (e.g., Minnesota 511) before driving.
Z13-P65:action3 Before stepping out during a sub-zero departure, execute quick home protection (shut main water valve if freezing is imminent, switch off stove/heaters, grab medications/IDs/pets, and text your out-of-area contact your destination).
Z13-P65:verify Confirm shelter destination is open (verify pet/accessibility accommodation), go-bags and meds packed, home shutoffs secured, and contact notified.
Z15-P02:action3 Treat an **EMERGENCY** tier (Tornado Emergency, Flash Flood Emergency, Evacuation Order) as an extreme life-threatening rare escalation demanding maximum immediate protective action or mandatory departure.
Z15-P05:stop Never drive into active law-enforcement road closures or live hazard zones trying to locate family—check in via the out-of-area contact and designated rally point.
Z15-P07:stop Extra evacuation lead time is non-negotiable for households with access needs—leave on early advisory/voluntary notices rather than waiting for final-hour orders.
Z15-P08:action1 Stage lightweight **grab-and-go bags** (one per person/family unit near an exit or car trunk) containing 72-hour essentials you can grab in under two minutes: water bottles, no-cook snacks, headlamp, NOAA/hand radio, phone power bank, rain/warm layers, basic first-aid kit, N95 masks, waterproof document pouch, cash, and 7-day spare medications.
Z15-P08:failure Packing all emergency supplies into one 90-pound plastic tub in the attic that cannot be lifted down stairs during a sudden midnight wildfire evacuation.
Z15-P08:verify Confirm go-bags are liftable in 2 minutes by their assigned carrier, stay-home bins are labeled separately, and 6-month refresh dates are logged.
Z15-P08:stop Never delay an urgent evacuation to pack bulky stay-home items—human life and compact go-bags leave first.
Z15-P15:action1 Monitor county emergency management, local AM/FM radio, or dial **211** (where active) as soon as a prolonged winter outage begins so you know exact community warming-center addresses, hours (daytime vs overnight), accessibility features, and pet policies BEFORE nightfall.
Z15-P15:action3 Shut off home space heaters/stoves, protect water lines if freezing is imminent, pack medications/chargers/warm bedding/IDs, and check in with your out-of-area relay upon arrival.
Z15-P15:verify Confirm shelter hours/overnight status verified, roads passable, home shutoffs secured, and medications/IDs/pets accounted for.
Z15-P23:action3 Remember that levees and dams reduce risk rather than eliminating it—any official levee-breach or dam-failure evacuation order demands instant high-ground departure with zero delay.
Z15-P23:verify Confirm home flood-zone status checked, two elevated exit routes mapped, and Flash Flood Warnings treated as instant high-ground triggers.
Z15-P27:action3 Park vehicles on verified high dry ground ahead of crest and evacuate early if authorities issue voluntary or mandatory flood evacuation orders.
Z15-P27:stop Rising water entering the basement or approaching exit roads halts all home-prep tasks immediately—evacuate safely to high ground.
Z15-P29:action1 Return ONLY after local officials declare the area safe, enter in **DAYLIGHT** using flashlights (zero matches/lighters), inspect exterior walls/foundation/porches for tilting, washed-out soil, or sagging ceilings BEFORE stepping inside, and exit immediately if you smell gas or hear hissing.
Z15-P30:action1 Learn the evacuation terms your locality uses before fire season. Stage documents, medications, pets and an accessible route early. Leave promptly when directed, using official routes.
Z15-P30:failure Waiting on the porch during a Level 2 "Set" advisory to see flames before loading the car, only to find smoke and fire trucks blocking the sole forest road.
Z15-P30:verify Confirm vehicle parked nose-out with fuel full during Set stage, go-bags/pets/meds loaded, and immediate departure on Go orders.
Z15-P30:stop Advancing flames, falling burning embers, or official Go orders override every property task—drive out immediately along official open routes.
Z15-P31:action2 Do NOT follow smartphone GPS "shortcut" detours onto narrow gravel forest roads or dead-end side streets—apps routinely route evacuees straight into active fire flanks or locked logging gates; obey live deputies, fire crews, and official DOT closures.
Z15-P31:action3 Once clear of the fire perimeter, check in with your out-of-area relay contact and official evacuation shelter registry, and NEVER attempt to drive back inside fire lines until authorities formally lift closures.
Z15-P31:failure Turning off a slow official evacuation highway onto a GPS-suggested forest shortcut that dead-ends behind burning timber.
Z15-P31:verify Confirm headlights on, windows shut, cabin air on RECIRCULATE, official open routes followed, and post-arrival check-in sent.
Z15-P34:action2 If your home lacks air conditioning (or power fails) during simultaneous smoke and extreme heat, relocate proactively to a public air-conditioned clean-air cooling center, library, mall, or cooled relative's home—taking vulnerable elders, infants, and asthmatics early.
Z15-P47:action1 Adopt the simple **"Half-Tank Is Empty"** rule year-round—refueling every household vehicle whenever gauges near half-full guarantees immediate 150-to-250+ mile evacuation range even if a sudden blackout shuts down every local gas station pump overnight.
Z15-P47:stop Driving an evacuation vehicle into an active disaster zone below quarter-tank without confirmed open fuel stations ahead risks stranding.
Z15-P50:action1 **EVACUATE IMMEDIATELY** whenever authorities issue a mandatory evacuation order, flames/floodwater threaten routes, indoor gas/CO/structural hazards occur, or prolonged utility loss pushes indoor heat/cold/medical batteries past safe floors while roads remain open.
Z15-P50:verify Confirm household checks official orders first, compares outdoor vs indoor lethality honestly, and revisits stay/go triggers as conditions shift.
Z15-P50:stop Official mandatory evacuation orders ALWAYS override personal preference to stay and guard property.
Z15-P51:action1 Highlight at least **TWO completely independent exit routes** leaving your neighborhood and town in opposite compass directions on a PAPER road map kept inside each vehicle—if a river bridge floods, a train derails, or a wildfire jumps the main highway, you immediately pivot to Route B without panic.
Z15-P51:action2 Drive both routes once in daylight during calm weather so every household driver recognizes intersections, low-lying flood bridges to avoid, and rural gravel dead-ends.
Z15-P51:action3 During an active disaster evacuation, **FOLLOW LIVE LAW-ENFORCEMENT OFFICERS, FIRE CREWS, AND OFFICIAL DOT ROAD CLOSURES—NOT SMARTPHONE GPS SHORTCUTS**, because crowdsourced traffic apps automatically divert drivers off congested main highways onto flooded side roads, downed-wire streets, or burning flanks.
Z15-P51:failure Letting a phone navigation app reroute an evacuating family off a slow county highway onto an unmonitored low-water creek bridge washed out by flash flooding.
Z15-P51:verify Confirm paper road map in every car with ≥2 opposite exit routes marked and every driver briefed to override GPS for live official closures.
Z15-P51:stop Any police barricade, downed wire, active smoke wall, or water across pavement halts forward travel immediately—turn back calmly to an open official corridor.
Z15-P52:action2 Run a verbal headcount at THREE fixed checkpoints: 1) before leaving the building, 2) inside the vehicle or at the neighborhood rally point, and 3) upon arriving at the shelter or out-of-town rally point—immediately texting status to your out-of-area relay contact.
Z15-P52:action3 Know exact school and daycare emergency reunification rules (official photo ID required, pre-listed backup authorized adults, designated off-site reunification center)—never rush an active emergency perimeter without following official reunification instructions.
Z15-P52:verify Confirm explicit buddy assignments, three-point headcount habit, updated school pick-up lists, and out-of-area relay number memorized/printed.
Z15-P53:action1 Check in through the shelter’s locally designated process and let your out-of-area contact know where you are if safe. Ask staff about accessibility and reunification support.
Z15-P53:action2 Bring personal medications, hearing/mobility aids, infant formula/diapers, pillow/blanket, phone chargers, and earplugs—remember general public shelters prohibit weapons, alcohol, illegal drugs, and personal cooking flames indoors.
Z15-P53:failure Refusing mandatory flood evacuation because of assuming no county pet-friendly shelter exists, or arriving without critical prescription medications.
Z15-P53:verify Confirm shelter registration completed, out-of-area relay notified, prescriptions carried on-person, and local pet-shelter options mapped beforehand.
Z15-P53:stop Acute medical symptoms, contagious vomiting/diarrhea, or depleted oxygen/dialysis supplies inside a general shelter must be reported immediately to the shelter nurse/manager.
Z15-P54:action1 Activate your **personal support network** (at least three trusted neighbors, relatives, or coworkers trained on how your mobility/medical equipment operates) early on Watch/Advisory notices rather than waiting until mandatory final-hour departures.
Z15-P55:action2 Practice loading nervous cats and dogs into carriers calmly during normal weeks and map pet-friendly motels, relatives, and county co-located animal shelters along BOTH evacuation routes ahead of disaster season.
Z15-P56:action1 Wait strictly for official county/city re-entry authorization (bringing photo ID and proof of address for law-enforcement checkpoints) and return in **DAYLIGHT** so structural damage, downed wires, and road washouts are clearly visible.
Z15-P56:failure Driving around a police checkpoint at dusk right after a flood or tornado and stepping straight into an energized flooded hallway.
Z15-P56:verify Confirm official all-clear received, daylight 360-degree exterior utility/structural check passed, damage documented visually, and kids/pets kept clear.
Z15-P61:action2 Use official county, Red Cross, National Guard, and municipal distribution hubs (PODs — Points of Distribution for water, MREs/groceries, ice, tarps, charging, and medical triage) proactively as soon as opened rather than waiting until home supplies are completely empty.
Z15-P62:action1 Recognize immediate exit or emergency triggers: serious illness, fire, a suspected internal gas leak, a CO alarm, or an official evacuation order. Contact 911 from safety. For dwindling medication or medical power, use a reserve margin set with the clinician or equipment provider and seek help early.
Z15-P62:action3 Leave while roads, daylight, fuel, and physical energy remain comfortably intact rather than waiting for all five red lines to converge simultaneously.
Z15-P62:stop Crossing ANY single objective red line activates orderly relocation or emergency-service assistance immediately.
Z15-P65:action2 Reinforce across every scenario that local jurisdictional alerts, law-enforcement road closures, county evacuation maps, and live NWS/fire/hazmat directives ALWAYS supersede generalized encyclopedia guidance—no draft text predicts site-specific disaster safety.

Z15-P06:failure Evacuating a wildfire or flood with zero paper IDs, zero prescription list, and $0 cash while regional card networks and cloud portals stay offline for four days.

Z15-P06:stop Never leave unencrypted sensitive identity files exposed in shared public spaces or hand personal banking info to unverified post-disaster solicitors.
Z15-P08:action1 Stage lightweight **grab-and-go bags** (one per person/family unit near an exit or car trunk) containing 72-hour essentials you can grab in under two minutes: water bottles, no-cook snacks, headlamp, NOAA/hand radio, phone power bank, rain/warm layers, basic first-aid kit, N95 masks, waterproof document pouch, cash, and 7-day spare medications.
Z15-P27:action1 Move vital documents, irreplaceable photos, medications, electronics, and hazardous basement chemicals (paints, fuels, pesticides—so floodwaters do NOT turn into toxic chemical soup!) up to upper floors well before flood crests arrive.
Z15-P27:failure Leaving 5-gallon gas cans, lawn pesticides, and vital home deeds on a basement shelf until floodwater lifts them and contaminates the entire house.
Z15-P27:verify Confirm basement chemicals/valuables moved high, sump pump checked, cars parked high, and early departure timed before roads flood.
Z15-P29:action2 Keep main electricity OFF until a licensed electrician/utility verifies wet panels, outlets, and submerged appliances are safe, do NOT drink municipal tap or private well water until utility/certified-lab clearance issues, and photograph all damage thoroughly for insurance/FEMA BEFORE stripping debris.
Z15-P42:action2 Build simple everyday habits that buffer cascading failures automatically: keep vehicle fuel above **HALF-TANK** year-round, maintain small-denomination cash, keep stored potable water and FIFO pantry food ready, and store critical phone numbers and medication lists on paper.
Z15-P42:failure Waiting until a regional derecho cuts power across five counties to drive on an empty gas tank to an ATM and grocery store.
Z15-P42:verify Confirm half-tank fuel habit, small cash staged, stored water independent of electric pumps, and paper contact binder ready.
Z15-P47:action2 Keep small-denomination physical cash ($1s, $5s, $10s, $20s) stored securely alongside vital documents so you can purchase food, ice, lodging, or fuel at generator-backed rural stores when broadband card terminals and ATMs stay dark.
Z15-P47:failure Waiting until a Hurricane/Blizzard Warning hits to queue at empty gas stations with 1/8 tank left and zero cash while card networks fail.
Z15-P47:verify Confirm household vehicles routinely refuel at half-tank, small cash bills staged safely, and zero fuel stored inside vehicle cabins/homes.
Z15-P54:action2 Pack a laminated **medical and communication summary card** (diagnoses, exact medications/doses, device wattage, allergies, primary clinician, and preferred communication method—e.g., ASL interpreter, large print, written pad) plus spare hearing-aid batteries, glasses, manual cane/chair backup, and labeled device chargers.
Z15-P56:action3 Photograph and video ALL exterior and interior damage thoroughly BEFORE moving debris or beginning cleanup for insurance and FEMA assistance, and keep children and pets safely away until broken glass, sewage, ash, and utility hazards are fully cleared.
Z15-P56:verify Confirm official all-clear received, daylight 360-degree exterior utility/structural check passed, damage documented visually, and kids/pets kept clear.
Z15-P57:action3 Transition cleanly into **Days 15–30 (Sustain & Recover):** Maintain health/morale routines, monitor reserve replenishment triggers with 48-hour buffers, coordinate mutual aid and county/FEMA assistance claims, and execute safe phased utility restoration as infrastructure returns.
Z15-P64:action1 Photograph and video EVERY damaged room, roof, basement waterline, vehicle, and ruined item clearly BEFORE discarding debris (keeping a small swatch of ruined carpet/flooring if insurance requests it), and save EVERY receipt for emergency lodging, tarps, fuel, food loss, and repairs in one dedicated folder.
Z15-P64:action2 Contact your homeowner/renter/auto insurer promptly AND verify whether county/state/FEMA disaster assistance declarations open via official `.gov` websites or 211—never pay upfront fees to anyone claiming to "expedite FEMA applications" (official federal/state disaster applications are ALWAYS free!).
Z15-P64:action3 Guard aggressively against post-storm contractor fraud: verify state contractor licenses, proof of insurance, written itemized estimates, and local references—NEVER sign blank insurance assignment forms or pay 100% cash upfront to unsolicited door-to-door crews right after hailstorms or floods.
Z15-P64:failure Throwing out flood-soaked appliances before taking photos, then paying $5,000 cash upfront to an unlicensed out-of-state storm-chaser who disappears.
Z15-P64:verify Confirm pre-cleanup damage photos saved, all emergency receipts kept together, official `.gov` assistance checked, and contractor licenses verified.
Z15-P64:stop High-pressure cash-upfront demands, refusal to show state license/insurance, or requests for bank passwords/FEMA fees terminate contact immediately and get reported to state authorities.

Z15-P57:action2 Shift purposefully into **Days 4–14 (Adapt):** Establish daily water/food/battery pacing logs, reliable sanitation and hygiene stations, neighborhood wellness check-ins, and safe resupply trips to county distribution hubs or open towns.
Z15-P57:action3 Transition cleanly into **Days 15–30 (Sustain & Recover):** Maintain health/morale routines, monitor reserve replenishment triggers with 48-hour buffers, coordinate mutual aid and county/FEMA assistance claims, and execute safe phased utility restoration as infrastructure returns.

Z03-P34:action1 Recognize that tree roots, deep pine duff and peat bogs hold oxygen and dry organic fuel below the surface—a fire built over duff or snow can burn downward unseen even after top ash looks gray.
Z03-P34:action2 Never bury a campfire solely with dirt or snow to put it out; burying insulates hot coals and roots so they continue smoldering underground and re-emerge in later wind.
Z03-P34:action3 Drown thoroughly with water, stir deep into the wet ash slurry, probe ring edges for buried steaming roots and repeat until every spot feels completely cool without wisps of steam or smoke.
Z03-P34:failure Shoveling dry sand or snow over glowing coals at checkout, leaving a buried root fire that flares into a wildfire two days later.
Z03-P34:stop If smoking soil or burning roots persist beneath a fire site despite watering, keep dousing if safe or report an active ground fire immediately to land managers or 911.
Z03-P35:action2 Recognize the opposite winter trap: once a fire melts down to ground level beneath snow, dry protected forest duff and roots underneath can ignite out of sight beneath overhanging snow shelves.

Z03-P44:action1 Schedule skills practice only on low fire-danger days with current legal authorization, calm wind and a cleared mineral-soil ring or fire-safe training tray well clear of dry fuels and structures.
Z15-P36:action1 Return ONLY after fire officials lift evacuation closures; walk carefully wearing thick leather boots, gloves, and N95 masks because gray ash heaps conceal **smoldering underground root embers and hot ash pits** capable of melting soles and causing deep burns weeks after flames pass.
Z15-P36:failure Letting children and pets run across soft gray ash in sneakers the morning after a neighborhood wildfire closure lifts.

exact_operational_assertions:
Z01-P22:action1 Watch for early failure cues—dimming headlamp, phone battery drop in cold, frozen water filter, jammed stove valve or torn shelter anchor.
Z02-P37:action3 Keep ALL synthetic fabrics and plastic sheets well away from stove flames, campfire sparks and hot coals—ultralight synthetics melt and ignite rapidly, causing severe burns.
Z02-P37:failure Pitching a nylon rainfly tightly in dry afternoon air without re-checking wet sag at night, letting wet fabric droop onto sleeping bags, or sparking a synthetic tarp near a stove.
Z02-P37:verify Identify your shelter's primary fabric class, check wet-tension adjustment access and confirm zero flame or spark sources operate nearby.
Z02-P50:failure Boiling snow on a canister stove inside a zipped tent vestibule during a storm, causing invisible odorless CO buildup or a flash fabric fire.
Z02-P50:verify Confirm zero fuel appliances, charcoal or open flames operate inside any shelter or vestibule and that all cooking runs outdoors downwind.
Z03-P19:action3 Keep portable stove fuel canisters, spare lighters, synthetic packs and shelter fabrics far away from open flame, radiant heat and popping embers.
Z03-P19:failure Stacking spare dry branches right beside the downwind edge of a fire ring or resting a butane canister next to coals to warm it up.
Z03-P19:verify Confirm fuel reserves stay dry, sit outside spark-fall distance and are physically separate from pressurized fuel bottles and camp gear.
Z03-P20:action1 Never pour gasoline, camp stove white gas, kerosene, alcohol or lighter fluid onto open flames, warm coals or unlit wood—invisible vapors pool and flash explosively back to the container.
Z03-P20:action2 Never toss empty or partial pressurized fuel canisters, aerosol cans or sealed containers into a campfire or hot ashes; trapped pressure ruptures violently with shrapnel and fireball risk.
Z03-P20:failure Squirt-squeezing stove fuel onto smoldering wet logs to speed ignition, igniting fuel vapors around hands and clothing.
Z03-P20:verify Confirm all liquid stove fuels and pressurized canisters remain capped and stored well away from the fire ring.
Z03-P20:stop If liquid fuel accidentally spills near a fire site, do NOT ignite anything there; evacuate the vapor zone and use a different safe site or no-fire plan.
Z03-P22:action3 Recognize that piezo-electric igniters can misfire at high elevation or in damp air, and never warm a cold lighter near open flame or hot stoves—pressurized fuel canisters can burst.
Z03-P28:action1 Check the local order for the exact stove type and permitted operation. A shutoff valve alone does not establish permission. Check the model temperature and fuel limits.
Z03-P28:action2 Match fuel and operating conditions to the stove instructions. This comparison does not establish that a given liquid-fuel stove will perform safely at a particular altitude or temperature.
Z03-P28:failure Taking an unregulated canister stove into 5°F winter air without testing cold output, or using an open alcohol stove during a Stage 2 shutoff-valve-only restriction.
Z03-P28:verify Confirm the stove matches local fire restriction rules (on/off valve requirement), forecast low temperature and manufacturer-approved fuel type.
Z03-P28:stop Never operate any stove indoors or in a tent vestibule, and never substitute unapproved fuels in a stove rated for a specific fuel.
Z03-P29:action1 Extinguish the stove completely and wait until the burner, windscreen and fuel tank feel cool before cracking open any fuel cap or pump assembly.
Z03-P29:action2 Refuel strictly outdoors on level bare ground well away from tents, campfires, lit stoves, smoking materials and food-preparation areas.
Z03-P29:action3 Wipe away any fuel drips, cap the supply bottle tightly and move the stove several steps away from any spilled ground fuel before attempting to light it.
Z03-P29:failure Cracking a warm stove pump open beside a companion's burning stove or lighting a fuel-soaked stove right over a fresh white-gas spill.
Z03-P29:verify Confirm stove body is cool, nearby ignition sources are out, fuel bottle is sealed and stove stands on clean dry ground away from drips.
Z03-P29:stop If fuel leaks from pump seals, hose threads or tank seams during pressurization, depressurize outdoors away from ignition and retire the stove from service.
Z03-P30:action1 Never wrap a tight full-enclosure foil windscreen around a canister-top stove—trapped radiant heat can overheat the pressurized fuel canister underneath and cause a catastrophic rupture.
Z03-P30:action2 Follow the exact model instructions. Some canister-top stoves explicitly prohibit all windscreens. Do not add or position a barrier that the instructions prohibit or that can redirect heat toward the fuel container.
Z03-P30:action3 Match pot diameter to stove arm limits and place the stove on a flat non-flammable surface so boiling pots cannot tip onto operators or dry needles.
Z03-P30:failure Wrapping heavy aluminum foil snugly around a threaded isobutane canister until the metal becomes too hot to touch.
Z03-P30:verify Confirm fuel canister stays cool to touch during operation, pot sits centered on stable supports and surrounding ground is cleared of dry needles.
Z03-P35:action3 Prefer a rated outdoor winter stove on a stable insulated base (such as a stove board per manufacturer guidance) over trying to maintain an open wood fire in deep winter snow.
Z03-P35:verify Confirm winter heat/boiling relies on a stable outdoor stove or an authorized cleared mineral-soil ring with full cold-ash verification.
Z03-P35:stop If melting snow collapses the fire bed or steam/smoke escapes beneath snowbanks, drown the remnants cold and shift to stove or no-fire insulation.
Z03-P38:action1 Watch and smell for liquid fuel seepage at bottle threads, hissing unlit canister valves, uneven yellow sputtering flames or sudden priming flare-ups before placing a pot on the burner.
Z03-P38:action2 If a stove flares high, keep face and hands back, turn off the fuel control valve ONLY if safely reachable without crossing flame—otherwise step back on clear ground and let contained residual fuel burn out safely while protecting nearby gear.
Z03-P38:action3 Never pour water directly onto a burning liquid-fuel pool (water spreads floating gasoline/white-gas flames); keep stoves strictly on cleared non-combustible surfaces outdoors.
Z03-P38:failure Grabbing a flaring liquid-fuel stove inside a vestibule to toss it outside, splashing burning fuel across clothes and tent nylon.
Z03-P38:verify Confirm tight leak-free fuel connections, steady blue controlled flame and unobstructed shutoff reach before cooking.
Z03-P38:stop Retire any leaking, damaged or persistently flaring stove immediately and switch to cold food, alternate water treatment or emergency assistance.
Z04-P27:action2 Add snow gradually in dense handfuls with the lid on to reduce wind cooling and fuel consumption, operating the stove strictly outdoors away from shelters.
Z04-P47:action1 Use only single-wall, unlined heat-safe metal vessels—never heat sealed bottles, vacuum-insulated flasks (which can rupture) or plastic containers over flame.
Z04-P47:action2 Check pot stability on stove supports or fire grates on level cleared outdoor ground so boiling water cannot tip onto legs or extinguish the burner with spilled fuel.
Z04-P47:action3 Keep all stove and fire boiling strictly outdoors away from tents, vestibules and vehicles, and use a pot lifter or insulated grip when removing hot lids.
Z04-P47:failure Placing a vacuum-insulated steel bottle on coals or balancing an oversized heavy pot on a narrow ultralight stove inside a tent vestibule.
Z04-P47:verify Confirm single-wall unlined metal construction, unsealed lid venting, level outdoor support and clear space around the hot zone.
Z04-P47:stop If the vessel is sealed, lined, unstable or the only sheltered space is enclosed, stop heating and use an alternate safe method or supply.
Z04-P48:stop Never warm frozen plastic bottles directly over open flame or stove burners; thaw safely in warm water or sheltered body/ambient heat.
Z09-P19:failure Skipping tight frapping turns between the poles, leaving a wobbly tripod that collapses when a water pot hangs from it.
Z09-P19:stop Never sleep beneath lashed deadfall roofs or treat camp lashings as engineered overhead structures; keep hot boiling pots stable and clear of legs.
Z12-P11:action1 Anticipate four major cold breakdowns: (1) alkaline and phone batteries lose capacity rapidly (prefer cold-rated lithium cells kept warm), (2) upright butane canisters lose vapor pressure, (3) wet hollow-fiber filters crack invisibly when frozen.
Z12-P11:action2 Anticipate mechanical cold brittleness: plastic pack buckles snap under sharp impact, frozen zippers jam on ice glaze, hydration hoses freeze solid and liquid white gas causes instant frostbite if spilled on bare skin.
Z12-P11:failure Discovering at −10°F that an upright canister stove barely flickers, the hydration tube is frozen solid and the wet water filter cracked overnight.
Z12-P11:verify Confirm lithium/warmed power, cold-capable stove/fuel, wide-mouth water carry, dry/protected filter or boiling plan and gentle buckle handling.
Z12-P35:action3 Keep stored water jugs, medications (such as insulin or epinephrine) and pressurized camp fuel canisters out of direct scorching sun and hot closed trunks where pressure and thermal spoilage spike.
Z13-P08:action3 Turn the generator completely OFF and allow the engine and muffler to COOL completely before opening the fuel cap or refueling—gasoline spilled onto a hot exhaust ignites explosively in seconds.
Z13-P08:failure Pouring gasoline from a jerrycan into a hot running generator in the dark to avoid interrupting the refrigerator, igniting a flash vapor fire.
Z13-P08:verify Confirm dry level open-air placement, intact GFCI cords clear of puddles, and engine completely shut off and cooled prior to fueling.
Z13-P21:action3 NEVER sleep with an unvented fuel-burning heater running, ALWAYS refuel outdoors after full cooldown, and keep working battery CO alarms active in the room and hallway.
Z13-P60:action1 Store gasoline, kerosene, and ALL pressurized propane cylinders (both 20-lb tanks and 1-lb green cylinders) STRICTLY OUTSIDE living spaces—NEVER inside basements, bedrooms, closets, or near water-heater/furnace pilot flames (heavier-than-air fuel vapors creep along floors and explode upon reaching ignition sparks).
Z13-P60:action2 Use ONLY approved, tightly sealed, properly color-coded safety fuel containers within local residential fire-code volume limits, kept upright in a cool shaded ventilated outdoor shed or exterior storage cabinet out of children's reach.
Z15-P47:action3 Never hoard gasoline in unapproved jugs, glass bottles, or inside car trunks/living quarters during storm panics—spilled fuel vapors ignite explosively from static sparks or rear-end collisions.
Z16-P32:action1 Open Z03-P28 for compare canister, liquid-fuel and solid-fuel stoves by temperature and altitude; Z03-P29 for refuel liquid stoves safely on cleared ground away from ignition.

Z01-P20:action1 Monitor wind direction, smoke plumes, storm outflow gusts and official evacuation notices to keep at least two exit paths open away from the hazard.
Z02-P40:failure Building a roaring fire close to a synthetic tarp or dry brush lean-to using a memorized step-count clearance and falling asleep while wind shifts sparks onto bedding.
Z03-P13:stop If wind gusts scatter sparks, fuel burns too large to manage or smoke blows across shelters, drown and stir the fire cold immediately.
Z03-P18:stop If gusts blow flames sideways out of the ring or fuel shifts unpredictably, stop adding wood and drown the fire completely.
Z03-P19:action1 Stack spare fuel well clear of the fire ring on the upwind or crosswind side—never downwind where floating sparks and embers land directly on dry kindling.
Z03-P19:failure Stacking spare dry branches right beside the downwind edge of a fire ring or resting a butane canister next to coals to warm it up.
Z03-P19:stop Move reserves farther back or extinguish the fire immediately if sparks reach staged wood or wind shifts toward camp gear.
Z03-P31:action3 Treat a Red Flag Warning (low humidity plus high wind) as an automatic stop to open flames—even where campfires are technically legal, sparks escape containment rapidly.
Z03-P31:failure Assuming a fire ring at a backcountry campsite means fires are currently allowed during a regional burn ban or Red Flag Warning.
Z03-P33:action1 Watch treetops, smoke angle and rising sparks—steady breezes or sudden gusts can carry glowing embers well beyond a cleared mineral ring into dry grass or needle beds downwind.
Z03-P33:action2 Recognize that fine dead fuels (cured grass, dry pine needles, birch bark curls) ignite within seconds during low relative humidity and spread faster uphill with wind alignment.
Z03-P33:action3 Keep water and a stirring tool staged outside the smoke path and cancel or drown any campfire the moment gusts lift sparks outside the ring perimeter.
Z03-P33:failure Leaving a crackling pine-wood fire unattended for five minutes while an afternoon breeze lifts glowing bark embers into dry grass ten yards downwind.
Z03-P33:verify Confirm calm controllable wind, zero escaping sparks and full downwind fuel scan before adding another stick.
Z03-P33:stop Any escaping spark into surrounding brush, rising gusts or active Red Flag conditions requires immediate fire extinguishment; if fire spreads beyond instant control, evacuate and call 911.
Z03-P43:action3 Rely on phone/satellite location reports and non-combustion signals whenever burn bans, wind or dry fuels make an open signal fire illegal or dangerous to the stranded party.
Z03-P43:failure Lighting a smoky brush fire in a dry forest to signal searchers, trapping the stranded group in a fast-moving wildfire.
Z03-P43:stop Never ignite a wildland fire as a signal; prioritize safe open visibility, audio/LED signaling and verified electronic contact when service permits.
Z03-P44:action1 Schedule skills practice only on low fire-danger days with current legal authorization, calm wind and a cleared mineral-soil ring or fire-safe training tray well clear of dry fuels and structures.
Z03-P44:stop Cancel or shut down training immediately if wind rises, humidity drops into Red Flag conditions, water runs low or any participant loses control of tools or flames.
Z11-P16:stop Never light uncontrolled brush fires as signals or step onto unstable ice/cliffs to improve visibility.
Z12-P73:action1 Recognize the dual drought hazard: parched fuels and low humidity create explosive wildfire spread (triggering Red Flag Warnings and strict fire bans), while hardened hydrophobic soils and burn scars turn sudden summer rain into violent flash floods and debris flows.
Z12-P73:failure Assuming a drought-parched canyon has zero flood hazard, or ignoring distant smoke plumes and Red Flag Warnings while camping down a single dead-end forest road.
Z15-P30:action2 Remember that wind shifts and spotting embers jump highways and change fire direction in minutes—if you feel unsafe or see thick advancing smoke/ash even BEFORE a formal Go order arrives, leave early on your own initiative.

Z01-P20:action2 Evacuate early along open official routes when wildfire approaches or Red Flag winds threaten your corridor; do not wait for flames or roadblocks.
Z01-P20:failure Waiting to pack nonessential camp gear while smoke thickens, wind topples trees or a single exit road closes behind the party.
Z01-P20:stop Never drive or walk through active flames, downed power lines, flooded crossings or zero-visibility smoke; follow emergency responder directions immediately.
Z02-P21:action2 For outdoor chemical releases or heavy wildfire smoke, follow official orders to close windows, shut off HVAC/ventilation intakes and move to an interior room until officials issue an all-clear.
Z02-P54:action1 Abandon tents and forested campsites immediately upon a Tornado Warning, Flash Flood Warning, approaching wildfire evacuation order or active tree/limb failures in rising gusts.
Z02-P54:stop When an abandonment trigger fires, prioritize human life over tents and gear—leave equipment behind rather than delaying exit into an active hazard.
Z02-P55:stop Never cross flooded roads, downed power lines, active flames or unverified ice during relocation; if trapped by a sudden hazard, take the safest available high/clear refuge and call 911.
Z03-P33:stop Any escaping spark into surrounding brush, rising gusts or active Red Flag conditions requires immediate fire extinguishment; if fire spreads beyond instant control, evacuate and call 911.
Z03-P39:action2 If a fire escapes instant control or an official wildfire evacuation warning arrives, abandon camp equipment immediately and evacuate upwind or crosswind along an open verified road or exit—do not stay to fight advancing wildland fire.
Z03-P39:action3 Call 911 as soon as safely clear to report exact location, wind direction, fuel type and any trapped people, and protect airways from heavy smoke indoors or per official guidance.
Z03-P39:failure Spending minutes trying to stomp out wind-driven grass flames with boots while smoke cuts off the sole trailhead road.
Z03-P39:verify Confirm all group members know the immediate evacuation route, rally point and 911 reporting details before any fire is lit.
Z03-P39:stop Life safety always overrides camp gear and fire fighting—never enter active flame corridors, dense blinding smoke or closed evacuation zones.
Z03-P43:failure Lighting a smoky brush fire in a dry forest to signal searchers, trapping the stranded group in a fast-moving wildfire.
Z10-P74:action1 Move away from dense wildfire smoke plumes promptly, reduce heavy aerobic exertion (which pulls deep PM2.5 particles into lungs), and relocate into an enclosed clean-air indoor room or outside the smoke corridor whenever possible.
Z10-P74:failure Running hard trails in Very Unhealthy wildfire smoke wearing a damp bandana under the false belief it blocks fine smoke and gases.
Z10-P74:stop Active advancing flames, thick eye/throat-burning smoke, chest pain, or worsening wheezing requires immediate evacuation and clinical evaluation.
Z11-P50:stop If immediate physical danger (rising flood, wildfire, falling timber, rockfall) threatens the spot, move calmly only the short distance needed to reach clear safe ground first, then execute STOP.
Z11-P52:action1 Ask Question 1 — **Is this exact spot immediately dangerous?** Active flash flood, wildfire, avalanche runout, falling timber, tidal cutoff or toxic fumes require moving immediately to the nearest safer clear ground.
Z12-P73:action2 Verify current fire restrictions, active wildfire smoke plumes and upstream storm cells before every dry-season trip, keeping two independent road or trail exits mapped.
Z12-P73:failure Assuming a drought-parched canyon has zero flood hazard, or ignoring distant smoke plumes and Red Flag Warnings while camping down a single dead-end forest road.
Z12-P73:stop Active Red Flag wildfire approach, heavy smoke, Flash Flood Warning or dry emergency water reserves trigger immediate early evacuation along open routes.
Z15-P30:action3 Never stay behind trying to defend a house with a garden hose when mandatory evacuation orders issue—wildland fire storms overwhelm municipal water pressure and trap stay-behind residents behind burning trees.
Z15-P31:stop If sudden fire blocks every route ahead with zero safe escape, turn around early if open—never drive straight into active flames or dense zero-visibility smoke walls.
Z15-P35:action1 Verify the respirator is stamped **NIOSH N95 or P100** with dual head straps (not loose single-loop dust masks, surgical masks, cloth gaiters, or bandanas, which leak fine PM2.5 smoke freely around the cheeks and nose).
Z15-P35:failure Wearing a damp cloth bandana or loose surgical mask while clearing storm brush in heavy wildfire smoke near active glowing ash.
Z15-P35:stop Dizziness, labored breathing inside a mask, or proximity to active flames/chemical fumes requires moving immediately indoors to clean air or evacuating.
